Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clear request. I knocked together a quick coverage scenario and attached the calculator (capacity_coverage_calculator.xlsx) plus a one-page projection that maps to your demand windows (gpu_mix_projection.pdf). Highlights up front:

- Baseline (off-peak) target: 35 rps aggregate, 64 tokens/request average => baseline compute = ~2.2k tokens/sec.
- Peak (holiday flash): 360 rps aggregate, same token mix => ~23k tokens/sec.
- Recommendation: start with a committed pool sized to cover ~70% of peak (comfortably covering expected committed business) plus a 15% burst lane for predictable surges. That equates to a mix of H100 80GB for latency-critical requests and A100 80GB for cost-effective steady throughput in the projection.

Fallback policy we propose: when the reserved pool is saturated, requests route to our shared-host tier (lower-priority) on L4 / T4-like GPUs with an automated model variant that reduces KV cache and applies 4-bit quantization where acceptable. We surface predicted latency degradation per path in the spreadsheet.

I put Rishi and Grace on-loop for the pack-sizing assumptions and ROI numbers — Rishi, could you confirm the utilization and failover padding? Grace, can you validate the organizational SLAs for canary rollover?

Next step: if this looks reasonable, we can run a 72-hour synthetic workload against a mirrored baseline to get empirical p95 figures before the commercial commit.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_coverage_calculator.xlsx, gpu_mix_projection.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Kim / Grace —

Quick confirmation of the numbers I used in the calculator:
- Token assumptions: 64 tokens per API call average, 8k token context for a small cohort of long queries (rare).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 200ms for the latency tier; p50 <= 80ms.
- GPU mapping used: H100 (best latency) -> 1x H100 covers ~600 requests/min with p95 ~170ms at 64 tokens; A100 -> ~420 req/min; L4 -> ~90 req/min (higher tokenization overhead).
- Utilization planning: we size reservations to 65–75% utilization to leave headroom for KV cache fragmentation and future growth. We include a 15% reserve for region failover and preemption scenarios.

Important note on shared fallback economics: when we route to shared hosts (L4), cost per token drops but p95 can increase 2–4x depending on burst. We included a modeled SLA credit exposure line item in the spreadsheet so finance can see tradeoffs.

If Sophie / procurement want, we can include a small SLO ladder: e.g., commit to 99.5% availability on reserved lanes, and offer credits if reserved-coverage drops below agreed thresholds during defined peak windows.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Products

Hi Sophie —

Appreciate the precise asks — pushed an alternate scenario into the same workbook (tab: A100-heavy). Summary of differences:

- A100-heavy profile: shift ~40% of latency-sensitive queries to optimized batching on A100. This reduces required H100 count by ~30% but increases projected p95 by ~30ms outside peak windows. Cost delta: ~-18% monthly on committed spend but slightly larger SLA exposure during very short spikes.
- Lead time: growing committed capacity is typically a 2–4 week operation once the commercial amendment is executed; temporary burst capacity on Hosted can be enabled within hours for controlled traffic.
- Regional failover: we strongly recommend a multi-AZ reservation with automated cross-AZ routing. If us-west AZ degrades, traffic routes to us-east reserved pool; we model a 12–18% added tail-latency for cross-region hops and include that in the failure runbook. For customers requiring <1% cross-region latency impact we recommend a mirrored reserved pool (higher cost).

Action items:
- Sophie: confirm which scenario (H100-balanced vs A100-heavy) you'd like modeled for final commercial terms.
- Sophie / procurement: if you want SLO ladders, we can add a simple credit band tied to reserved-coverage for holiday peak windows.

I'll queue a short 30-min sync with Rishi & Grace next week to walk through the workbook if helpful.

Thanks —
Kim
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
